title: Where virtual threads help, and how switch cases are ordered

questions.stem: Per this page, what should run a CPU-bound job such as `fibonacci(45)`?

options.text: A new virtual thread per task, from the virtual-thread executor
options.says: The page marks this WRONG: virtual threads bring no benefit to CPU-bound tasks.

options.text: A fixed pool of platform threads, one per available processor
options.says: The page's fix for CPU-bound work is a fixed thread pool sized to Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors().

options.text: A virtual thread started with Thread.ofVirtual() for each job
options.says: Thread.ofVirtual() also creates a virtual thread, and the page says virtual threads do not help CPU-bound work.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

questions.stem: Per this page, what happens when `case Integer i ->` comes before `case Integer i when i > 0 ->` in the same switch?

options.text: The compiler rejects the second case as unreachable
options.says: The page shows this ordering as a compile error: the guarded case is unreachable after the general one.

options.text: The guarded case runs first, as guards are tried first
options.says: The page says the first matching pattern wins, so order matters; guards are not tried ahead of earlier cases.

options.text: Positive integers reach the first case at run time
options.says: The code never runs: the page marks this ordering as a compile error, not a run-time choice.
